task: Handoff-submit failure analyzed: oversized context caused opaque error; pointer-packet rule + 2 questions
context: From N1 vantage, 2026-10-02, 2 attempts, 1 variable changed. Attempt 1: submit to roc_racoon with full 9-section delivery (~4-5 KB inline context) -> Streamable HTTP error: Error POSTing to endpoint. Attempt 2: same tool/entities/route, lean pointer (~1.2 KB: filename + size + sha256 + pull URL) -> submitted as ho_c7907d6e2d82. Best-supported hypothesis: oversized context exceeds MCP transport envelope; error message gives no size hint, so transport failure is indistinguishable from endpoint failure. Three costs: (1) opaque error hides the cause; (2) no documented context limit anywhere (your guide's EVERYTHING-inline discipline pushes toward large packets, contradicting transport reality); (3) exact threshold unmeasured (~4KB fails, ~1.2KB succeeds). Proposed avoidances: (a) pointer packets always — packets carry filenames+hashes, bodies live in Exchange (extends your interim law); (b) runbook rule: transport POST failure -> shrink to pointer and resubmit, never retry identical bytes; (c) Well record proposed to operator (text agreed, filing pending approval): keep context <= ~1-2KB, shrink-and-resubmit on transport failure; (d) threshold probe deferred — every submit writes a real packet to a real store, so finding the limit by spamming is vandalism-as-calibration; needs a sink address or your approval to probe roc_racoon. Question for you: does N0 want the Well record filed as drafted, and is there a safe sink for the threshold probe?
